newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mixed, nearbys up on corn, funds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mixed, nearbys up on corn, funds.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended mixed on Tuesday with nearbys up in line with gains in corn and on commercial and fund buying, traders said.
Traders said Cargill Inc and ADM Investor Services each sold one million bushels of March on the open which traders said was to hedge sales of producer and/or elevator stocks.
But both were said to be net buyers on the day.
Refco Inc bought at least 7.5 million bushels March and 1.5 million May on the day, traders said.
Soybeans were pressured early by forecasts for rain in the key Brazilian soybean region of Rio Grande do Sul.
But Brazilian sources told Reuters the rains would likely miss parched growing regions in the south.

"We can't talk about any drop in the harvest at this stage but if this drought continues for another 10 days, we could lose 10 to 15 percent of the crop," a spokesman for Brazil's agriculture department told Reuters on Tuesday.
The market remained underpinned by Friday's cut by USDA in its estimate for 1996-97 U.S. soybean ending stocks and on uncertainty about the fate of the South American soybean crop.
Soybeans closed two cents per bushel lower to one cent higher with March up 1/4 at $7.37.
Volume was estimated by the CBOT at 65,000 contracts, below Monday's actual volume of 83,881 contracts.
